surfaces.part: fir foliage tiers (stacked conical tiers with snow dusting)

answer.evidence: The fir is a conical silhouette whose width grows steadily from 2px at row 1 to 28px at row 40. The widening is interrupted by small notches at rows 14, 23-24 and 33. These notches mark the tier outlines but no horizontal surface is drawn. Each tier is shaded as one continuous face, with a lighter left side and a darker right side, so it reads as a vertical elevation. Snow patches (white pixels) sit on the branches, but they are scattered dustings and not a flat top band with a front-edge line or eave shadow. There is no ellipse and no roof plane. The trunk at rows 42-46 is 4px wide and has no top. The drawing is a front elevation of a stylised tree, with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small snow-dusted fir, and the references are broadleaf trees, so the kind matches (tree) and I judged structure only. The canopy has about 4 green steps from deep to light, plus snow highlights, and a brown trunk. That is about 5 steps, a little under Beodeul's 5-6. The outline is a dark green that leans visibly toward the canopy, not a neutral black line, which agrees with 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels. Tier edges are broken up by value, and the snow patches sit on the branch tiers as clumps. The 0% near-flat coverage matches this, so there are no flat fills. The measured 10 visible tones per tile is above reference tree-1a786c (7) and well below tree-d43edd (29). By eye the candidate sits between them: less lush than the big oak, but not thinner or more sticker-like than the smaller reference. A conifer is naturally simpler than a broadleaf canopy, so the lower density is acceptable.

surfaces.part: fir foliage tiers with snow dusting

answer.evidence: A conifer drawn as a stacked triangular silhouette (widths grow from 2 at row 1 to 28 at row 40) with a small trunk at rows 42-46. The foliage is lit on the left and shaded dark green on the right, and white snow patches sit on the branch tips. There is no horizontal top surface: no front-edge line with eave shadow, no ellipse and no visible contents. The tiers are drawn as flat frontal faces, and the snow patches are 1-2 row highlights, not a top plane. The tree reads as a front elevation.

surfaces.part: foliage tiers (conical fir body with snow flecks)

answer.evidence: The fir is a symmetric stepped triangle whose width grows from 2 px at row 1 to 28 px at row 40. The tiers have jagged bottom edges with dark shading (rows 40-41), but no tier has a band, ellipse or visible horizontal plane seen from above. The white snow patches are small scattered flecks along the slopes, not a flat top surface with a front-edge line. The right side is darker shading on the same front face, not a receding side face. The trunk (rows 42-46, 4 px wide) is a plain vertical strip. The whole object is a front elevation of foliage with no horizontal top surface.
